note: Every palette is six colours a piece and a cell can both be drawn in, so what matters is that no two are confusable — including for the roughly one man in twelve with a red-green colour deficiency. Deficiencies flatten hue and leave lightness alone, so separation is bought by spreading the six in lightness rather than by spacing them evenly in hue. `core` and `key` are the glyph interior and its keyline, shared by every palette. Switch palette by changing `default`. Measured by tools/palette.js, which simulates each deficiency and reports the closest pair.

trace.name: Trace
trace.note: Six hues evenly spaced and close in weight. The most colourful of the set and the least separable: its closest pair is green against cyan.

deep.name: Deep
deep.note: Muted, and free to spread in lightness — which is where its separation comes from. The widest margin of any palette here, at the cost of green reading pale and magenta dark.

even.name: Even
even.note: Muted, but held to a narrow lightness range so the six read as one set. Buys less separation than Deep and looks closer to Trace.

legible.name: Legible
legible.note: The Okabe-Ito palette (jfly.uni-koeln.de/color), chosen and verified by its authors to stay distinguishable under every colour deficiency. Keeps the six slot names, but they are orange, sky, blue-green, yellow, blue and vermilion.
